headline: Radar Fix Game - World Map Clue Challenge for ESL Lessons
outcomes: Students practise geography, place vocabulary, and clue interpretation through a live map challenge
Observation and reasoning become speaking prompts as students explain why a location fits the clues
The world-map format gives travel, culture, and current-events lessons a visual anchor
Teachers get a memorable review game that feels different from another multiple-choice quiz
howItWorks: LessonCaptain presents destination clues connected to cities, airports, landmarks, or world regions
Students use their devices to make a location guess or discuss the most likely answer
The teacher reveals the correct radar fix on the shared world map
The class compares guesses, explains clues, and collects points for close or accurate reasoning
teacherUseCases: Travel English lessons where students need to describe places, routes, and cultural clues
World Flight sessions where a map-based game reinforces the journey theme
Current-events or geography lessons where students practise making evidence-based guesses

faq.q: Is Radar Fix only for geography classes?
faq.a: No. Geography is the frame, but the language work is broader: students describe evidence, compare possibilities, use place vocabulary, and explain their reasoning in English.
Yes, if the teacher keeps the clues simple. Beginners can work with country names, directions, weather, and landmark vocabulary, while stronger students can handle cultural and historical clues.

faq.q: Does every student answer at the same time?
faq.a: The game is built for live participation. Depending on the class, students can submit individual guesses or discuss a team answer before the teacher reveals the map position.

faq.q: How does Radar Fix connect to World Flight?
faq.a: It fits naturally into a flight-themed lesson because the class is already thinking about destinations. Use it before arrival, after a city briefing, or as a quick culture review.

faq.q: How do students submit guesses in Radar Fix?
faq.a: No. Students join through a shared browser link and participate from any device without creating an account.
